Contract.title: An approval authorizes execution; holding a change for a batch is not a kernel state
Contract.Problem: The approval record carries a second decision, executes, with its own status value "approved for execution" beside "approved", a later Execution element, and the refusal "approval does not authorize execution". The owner ruled on 2026-11-13 that this state is useless: approved means the change can be executed, and "do not execute now" means hold it until a batch is run, a scheduling instruction with no decision behind it. Two pilot changes stand refused today for lack of a word nobody needed to record.
Contract.Change: An approval authorizes execution. The schema keeps the executes attribute and the Execution element as optional for records already written, and the kernel ignores both; a new record carries neither. The authorization states are unapproved, approved, rejected and altered after approval; among approval reasons run refuses only "no approval for revision n", and the phrase "approval does not authorize execution" is removed everywhere, as is the defect that a rejected approval must say executes="false". The brief's closing line and the prepare skill ask the owner for one statement, approve or reject with the reason, and say that an approval worded to defer the start, such as "approved, hold", is an approval the agent does not act on until the owner starts the change or a batch, and is recorded nowhere; the execute skill requires the state approved. authorization.md, commands.md, conformance.md, m2-proposal.md and the ledger entry L-05 are rewritten to this. The conformance cases that asserted the second state are replaced by cases that an approval without the attribute runs, that a record with executes false or an Execution element runs the same, and that the removed phrase and status value are never printed. The version becomes 0.6.0, with a 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 step that refreshes the installed skills and touches no change; this repository's pin is written to 0.6.0 by this change directly.

Constraints.Constraint: What an approval binds is unchanged: the contract hash, each check definition, the brief the owner read and the owner's words; only the second decision goes.
No record is rewritten; every approval record already written, in this repository and in a pilot, validates against the amended schema and authorizes execution under the new rule.
L-05 is amended to drop the execution decision from its mechanism, benefit and cost; no entry is added.
The surface shrinks by one status value and one refusal phrase and grows by nothing.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Any record of a hold: the kernel does not know whether an approved change is waiting for a batch.
The orchestrated run, which another change defines; it selects on approval alone once this change is in.
Upgrading any pilot repository, that is a repository other than this one that has adopted the kernel; each does it on the owner's flag.

Acceptance.Criterion: A change whose current revision has an approval runs and closes whether its record carries executes true, executes false, an Execution element or none of them, and the removed phrase and status value never appear; each is a conformance case with a test that fails when the kernel lacks it.
Every example and every closed change of this repository, whose approval records carry the attribute, still validates.
The kernel type-checks, the examples still verify, the generated packages carry the version of package.json, and neither they nor the CLI reference drift from their sources.
The kernel reports grace5 0.6.0 and this repository's pin reads 0.6.0.

A clone of this repository at tag v0.2.0 with one open change added, upgraded by the new kernel, lists the same changes with the same hashes, carries the pin 0.6.0, and leaves the open change's candidate as it was.

Automated.Command: bun -e "const fs = require('fs'); const out = require('child_process').execFileSync('bun', ['src/cli.ts', '--version']).toString().trim(); const pin = fs.existsSync('.grace5/kernel-version') ? fs.readFileSync('.grace5/kernel-version', 'utf8').trim() : ''; process.exit(out === 'grace5 0.6.0' && pin === '0.6.0' ? 0 : 1)"

Decisions.Decision: Approved means the change can be executed; "do not execute now" means hold it for a batch, a scheduling instruction and never a recorded state. Owner, 2026-11-13.
Old approval records keep their attribute and validate; the kernel reads every approval as authorization. No pilot record is rewritten; a pilot takes the rule with grace5 upgrade.
This change takes the cheap path the owner asked for on 2026-11-13: the brief and the review are written by the lead, marked self, and no subagent is used.

The version is 0.6.0, tagged v0.6.0 when this change closes; the change executes on master in the home repository while C-0007-orchestrate-skill, another session's draft, stays open and protected; no branch is created.

Owner, 2026-11-14: "no timeout tests any more. close the issue finally I ASK THIRD TIME!" The FL-09 wall-clock timeout test and its conformance declaration are removed; the runtime budget mechanism is unchanged.

Author's proposal for approval in revision 2: CK2 runs the focused approval, legacy-record upgrade, skill-refresh and bound-check amendment cases, with a 120-second budget, instead of the entire conformance suite. The other five checks, release behavior and write boundary are unchanged. Closure does not claim a fresh full-suite pass.
